clause: Compression, vanishing orthogonal part, rank-one products, normalized projector and converse
draft_quote: the identity $(I-P_y)AP_x=0$ places $Ax$ on the line of $y$
evidence_or_owed: The compression identity, the vanishing orthogonal part, the rank-one product and the formula for the output projection are stated, with the converse for a nonzero image.

clause: Norm and two positive products of the restriction
evidence_or_owed: Displayed. The text adds that the bounded adjoint of the restriction extends the product of the input projection with the adjoint of A, with an example in which the output reference vector lies outside the domain of that adjoint.

clause: Unique factor, modulus, forward and adjoint vector actions
evidence_or_owed: The modulus is displayed. The line map has the kernel of the restriction, the polar decomposition with that property is unique, and both vector actions are stated.

clause: The bridge and its positive coefficient fix the line orientation
draft_quote: among them $AP_x=aw$ with $a>0$ holds for $w=u_0$ only
evidence_or_owed: The partial isometries between the two lines are the phase multiples of the line map, and the bridge with a positive coefficient holds for one of them. A common phase of the two representatives leaves it unchanged.

clause: Anti-aligned companion of the restricted reference map
evidence_or_owed: The graph lines of the line map are defined at every phase under the weak bridge alone, and the aligned and anti-aligned lines are named.

clause: Total and maximal neutrality of both lines inside the ground plane
draft_quote: Each line is its own Krein-orthogonal complement in $\mathcal K_0$ and so is a maximal neutral subspace of the plane.
evidence_or_owed: The Krein product of a graph vector with a general vector of the plane is computed. It vanishes exactly on the line. The plane itself is not neutral.

clause: Both vectors have Hilbert norm one, zero Krein square, and half weight in each sector
draft_quote: Every $z^0_\varphi$ has Hilbert norm one, zero Krein square, and squared norm $1/2$ in each sector.
evidence_or_owed: Stated for every phase, with the normalized sector components.

clause: Trivial sector intersections and bijective coordinate projections of the aligned ground graph
draft_quote: A line $\mathcal N^0_\varphi$ meets each sector in zero only, and each coordinate projection maps it bijectively onto the corresponding reference line.
evidence_or_owed: Stated for every phase. A vector of the line is fixed by either component, and neither component is a vector of the line.

clause: Ground reflection, complex structure, and phase operator supported on the reference plane
evidence_or_owed: The reflection and the complex structure of the line map are displayed as operators that vanish off the plane. The phase operator is written as minus i times the complex structure, as in Section 3.

clause: Adjoints, grading, squares, and Pauli products of the three reference-plane operators
draft_quote: They satisfy $\mathcal R_0^*=\mathcal R_0$, $\mathcal R_0^2=P_{xy}$, $J\mathcal R_0=-\mathcal R_0J$, $\mathcal I_0^*=-\mathcal I_0$ and $\mathcal I_0^2=-P_{xy}$.
evidence_or_owed: Adjoints, squares and the anticommutation with the grading are stated. The three operators are the Pauli matrices in the basis of the two reference vectors, with the three products written out.

clause: Reflection eigenlines; action of J and of the complex structure on both signs
evidence_or_owed: Displayed for both vectors, with the projection onto the line at a general phase and the three means.

clause: Ground-line Witt pair
evidence_or_owed: The Hilbert product, the two Krein squares and the Krein cross product are displayed, and the pair is named.

clause: Entire projective neutral cone of the reference plane as a circle, including its two reflection eigenlines
draft_quote: The neutral rays of the plane form a circle with coordinate $\varphi$.
evidence_or_owed: Proved from the two conditions on the coefficients. Equal sector weights define the circle and the bridge selects one point on it.

clause: Aligned and anti-aligned rays have identical sector compressions
draft_quote: The sector components of $z_-$ lie on the rays of $x$ and of $y$, as do those of $z_+$ and of every $z^0_\varphi$.
evidence_or_owed: Stated for every point of the circle. The points differ in relative phase only, have equal means for every operator commuting with the grading, and equal mean energy under sector Hamiltonians with the reference vectors as eigenvectors.

clause: Two-sided compressions of reflection and complex structure and inclusion of the anti-aligned line
evidence_or_owed: Under strong compatibility the plane reduces both polar operators to the plane operators and every graph line of the line map lies in the corresponding full graph. The proposition proves these as equivalences. Under the weak bridge alone the compressions are the plane operators times the square root of the ground fidelity.

clause: Closed graph range and full adjoint formula
evidence_or_owed: The adjoint is displayed for the active carrier and described for the full output space. The range is closed because the graph map is an isometry on a complete space, also when the range of A is not closed.

clause: Special cases for the aligned and anti-aligned projections
evidence_or_owed: Both projections are displayed with their product, their sum and the resulting orthogonal decomposition of the active carrier. The replacement of the identity on the full direct sum is stated.

clause: Conjugation of rank-one projections and equality of their trace overlaps
evidence_or_owed: Displayed: the transport of a rank-one projection is the projection of the transported vector, and the two trace overlaps equal the squared modulus of the inner product.

clause: Spectra and bounded functional calculus
draft_quote: Hence $X$ and $VXV^*$ have the same spectrum, the second taken as an operator on $D$.
evidence_or_owed: The resolvent is transported, so the spectra agree on D. Polynomials and bounded Borel functions of a normal operator are transported, and positive operators, effects and projections keep their kind.

clause: Unit of the selected pair algebra
draft_quote: $\iota(I_S)=I_S\oplus I_D$ is the identity of $\mathcal K_A$
evidence_or_owed: The image of the input identity is the identity of the active carrier and the active projection after extension by zero.

clause: Normal faithful unital maximal representation, faithful selected restriction, and isomorphisms onto both sectoral algebras
draft_quote: The paired algebra $\iota(\mathcal M)$ is therefore isomorphic to $\mathcal M$ through the upper block and to $V\mathcal MV^*$ through the lower one.
evidence_or_owed: The map is linear, multiplicative, adjoint-preserving, unital, injective through its upper block and normal through both blocks. The restriction to a selected algebra and the two isomorphisms are stated.

clause: Graph compression identity
evidence_or_owed: Displayed, with the invariance of every graph. The text adds that a block-diagonal operator maps a graph into itself exactly when it is paired.

clause: Spectral measure of the transported observable
evidence_or_owed: Displayed, with the argument from uniqueness of the spectral measure. The text adds the unbounded self-adjoint case and the spectral measure of the extension by zero to the full output space.

clause: Four blocks of the graph density operator
evidence_or_owed: All four blocks are displayed, with the opposite phase factors in the two off-diagonal blocks.

clause: Diagonal blocks of a mixed graph state
draft_quote: Its compressions to the two sectors are $\tfrac12\rho$ and $\tfrac12V\rho V^*$.
evidence_or_owed: Both compressions, their traces and their normalizations are stated. Deleting the off-diagonal blocks gives the equal mixture of the graph states at two opposite phases.

clause: Meaning of the sector compressions of a graph density
draft_quote: the lower block $\tfrac12V\rho V^*$ is a compression and is not the reduced state of a subsystem
evidence_or_owed: The partial trace over the sector coordinate returns the input density with trace one and is what the paired observables read. A sector compression keeps one diagonal block with trace one half. The carrier is a direct sum of sectors and not a tensor product of two systems.

clause: Factorized ranges and projectors
draft_quote: the graph $\mathcal N_\varphi$ is $\ket{\varphi}\otimes S$, and $\Pi_\varphi$ is $\ket{\varphi}\!\bra{\varphi}\otimes I_S$
evidence_or_owed: In the sector coordinates the graph, its projection and the graph state of a density operator are written as products with the sector vector at the given phase.

clause: Ground, differentiated paired space, and adjoint kernel under the weak bridge
evidence_or_owed: Displayed with the corresponding split of the complement of the output reference vector. The middle part is paired by the polar map with the complement of the partner in the initial support.
